title: Binomial higher Leibniz rule for a Lie derivation
statement:
Let $L$ be a Lie algebra over $\mathbf Q$ [def-wf-lie-algebra], with no dimension assumption. Let $D:L\to L$ be a $\mathbf Q$-linear map satisfying $D([x,y])=[D(x),y]+[x,D(y)]$ for all $x,y\in L$. Write $D^0=\operatorname{id}_L$ and $D^n$ for $n$-fold composition. Then for every $n\in\mathbf N$ and $x,y\in L$,
$$D^n([x,y])=\sum_{i=0}^{n}\binom ni[D^i(x),D^{n-i}(y)].$$
Here $\binom ni$ acts by its image in $\mathbf Q$; no nilpotence hypothesis on $D$ is imposed.
